title: On the Gas Content, Star Formation Efficiency, and Environmental Quenching of Massive Galaxies in Protoclusters at z ≈ 2.0-2.5
question: What are the gas content, star formation efficiency and environmental quenching of massive galaxies in two proto-clusters at z=2.10 and 2.47, compared with field galaxies?

what.value: Field control sample and gas scaling relations (ALMA Band 7, ~55 targets)

evidence.quote: The adopted field scaling relations comes from (cite: Scoville2016a)
drawn from (cite: Casey2015a; Casey2016a); and (cite: Hung2016a)

evidence.loc: 3.2 Stellar masses and star formation rates
evidence.quote: We use the COSMOS2015 catalog ((cite: Laigle2016a)
This estimation assumes a volume of $15000\,\rm cMpc^3$ for each structure, as estimated by (cite: Casey2016a).

recipe.method: Natural-weighted continuum images; peak-finding within 1 arcsec of optical positions on primary-beam corrected maps; 3 sigma threshold
key_parameters: local noise = 68th percentile of pixel distribution

recipe.method: Weighted average of image cutouts; weights inverse square of noise; peak within 1 arcsec of center
Scoville et al. 2016 calibration of RJ dust continuum to ISM mass
MAGPHYS SED fitting of COSMOS2015 photometry plus ALMA, fixed spectroscopic redshift, BC03, Chabrier IMF, delayed exponential SFH

recipe.goal: Compare SFE, gas fractions and quenching with field
recipe.method: KS test on SFE vs field; gas fraction f_gas=Mmol/(Mmol+M*); detection fraction vs field; quenching efficiency and timescale from stellar age
assumptions: Planck cosmology H0=68, OmegaLambda=0.69; Chabrier IMF

evidence.loc: 2.2 ALMA observations and detection of dust continuum
evidence.quote: From all the 68 proto-cluster galaxies which lie within our surveyed area, 19 sources were detected above our adopted threshold

answer_key.quantity: KS probability SFE same as field (M*>1e10)

evidence.quote: we derive a probability of $p=0.81$ that both of them are drawn from the same parent distribution
we estimate an average quenching efficiency of $\epsilon_q=0.45^{+0.16}_{-0.13}$
resulting in an upper limit on quenching timescale of $\tau_q<1\,\rm Gyr$

answer_key.quantity: Gas fraction of massive gas-poor galaxies

evidence.quote: some of the most massive galaxies studied in this work show very low gas mass fractions, $f_{\rm gas}\lesssim 6-10\,\%$

not_stated_but_needed: Number and parameters of CLEAN iterations/threshold and masking
MAGPHYS priors and settings, star formation history parameters
How passive and star-forming fractions and their errors were computed for the quenching efficiency
Field detection fractions binned by mass used in Figure 7
missing_for_reproduction: Field comparison data digitized from Scoville2016, Bouwens2016, Dunlop2017
score_reason: Public data and a simple method but several parameters (imaging, SED setup, fraction calculations) unstated.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple continuum flux to mass recipe with numeric tables, though SED parts need external photometry.
